quote.translation: And when Lange writes in his History of Materialism that "no two things contradict each other so completely as chance and necessity, and nevertheless there is nothing else that is so often confused as the two" (Lange, Geschichte des Materialismus, I. S. 13), this too is because the combination of causal necessity with teleological contingency on the one side, and of teleological necessity with causal contingency on the other, so readily comes about.

regions.text: いまこの結合の仕方を假りに「異種結合」を名付けて置かう。

quote.translation: Let us provisionally call this way of combining "heterogeneous combination".

regions.text: しかし、異種結合だけが可能約な結合の仕方である解ではない。

quote.translation: Heterogeneous combination is not, however, the only possible way of combining.

regions.text: 因果的必然性と目的々必然性とが結合して、必然性を強調する哲學となり因果偶然性と目々偶然性とが若合して偶然性を力説する哲學を構・成する場合もある。

quote.translation: Causal necessity and teleological necessity may also combine to form a philosophy that emphasises necessity, and causal contingency and teleological contingency may combine to constitute a philosophy that stresses contingency.

regions.text: ストア派は目々必然性から後して因果必然性に重る徹底的な決定論を説き（二九三貫参照、エビクロスは因果的偶然性から出て目的偶然性に終る一義的な非決定論を唱へた（一一五ー一一六貫、一二七貫急照）。かういふ結合の仕方を同種若合」と名付けることが出來る。これらの關係を上のやうな図形によつて現はして見よう。

quote.translation: The Stoics taught a thoroughgoing determinism that starts from teleological necessity and arrives at causal necessity (see p. 292), and Epicurus advocated a univocal indeterminism that sets out from causal contingency and ends in teleological contingency (see pp. 115-116, 127).
